summary: Assess climate hazards, map infrastructure exposure, and prioritize adaptation actions. Explore this practical five-day course.
lede: Physical climate risk assessment for infrastructure examines how climate hazards may affect assets and the services they provide. For infrastructure planners, engineers, asset managers and climate-risk analysts, the course covers mapping asset exposure with GIS, assessing vulnerability and potential consequences, and documenting data assumptions. Participants also practise creating prioritized risk registers and comparing adaptation actions to support planning and investment decisions.
audienceIntro: Climate risk assessment training is designed for professionals who evaluate physical climate hazards across infrastructure and service assets. It suits those working with asset inventories, GIS information, risk evidence, adaptation planning, or investment decisions. This course is designed for: Climate-risk analysts screening hazards and documenting asset-level vulnerability. Utility planners assessing climate threats to water and energy services. Infrastructure asset managers prioritizing maintenance and adaptation investments. Civil and infrastructure engineers reviewing climate-sensitive design assumptions. GIS analysts mapping asset locations against climate hazard data. Insurance risk analysts assessing physical climate exposure across asset portfolios. Public investment analysts evaluating climate risks in infrastructure proposals. Development-finance practitioners incorporating physical climate risk into project appraisal. Climate adaptation officers translating risk findings into asset-level actions. Infrastructure resilience leads reporting climate exposure and adaptation priorities to executives.
prerequisites: No prior climate-risk modelling or coding is required. Familiarity with infrastructure assets, asset inventories, or GIS data is useful; exercises focus on assessment and interpretation rather than programming.
